item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 180504
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Sat Oct 17 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Trudy, located offshore of southwestern Mexico.

South of Southern Mexico:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form well offshore of
southern Mexico within a couple of days. Environmental conditions
appear conducive for gradual development thereafter, and a tropical
depression is likely to form around the middle of next week while
it moves westward to west-northwestward, well south of Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...80 percent.

$$
Forecaster Hagen

item.title: Hurricane Trudy Public Advisory Number 19a
item.description:
Issued at 1200 AM CST Sun Oct 18 2026 
000
WTPZ31 KNHC 180532
TCPEP1
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Trudy Intermediate Advisory Number 19A
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP212026
1200 AM CST Sun Oct 18 2026
 
...TRUDY BRINGING HEAVY RAINS AND STRONG WINDS TO PORTIONS OF 
SOUTHWEST AND WEST-CENTRAL MEXICO...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1200 AM CST...0600 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...18.5N 106.1W
ABOUT 115 MI...185 KM WSW OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
ABOUT 135 MI...215 KM S OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...100 MPH...155 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 325 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...976 MB...28.82 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
None.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Hurricane Warning is in effect for...
* The coast of Mexico from Manzanillo northward to Cabo Corrientes
 
A Hurricane Watch is in effect for...
* The coast of Mexico from south of Manzanillo to Punta San Telmo
 
A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for...
* The coast of Mexico from south of Manzanillo to Punta San Telmo
* The coast of Mexico from north of Cabo Corrientes to San Blas
* Las Islas Marias
 
A Hurricane Warning means that hurricane conditions are expected
somewhere within the warning area. Preparations to protect life
and property should be rushed to completion.
 
A Hurricane Watch means that hurricane conditions are possible
within the watch area, in this case within 12 hours.
 
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected somewhere within the warning area within 12 hours.
 
Interests elsewhere in southwestern and west-central Mexico should
continue to monitor the progress of Trudy.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1200 AM CST (0600 UTC), the center of Hurricane Trudy was located 
near latitude 18.5 North, longitude 106.1 West. Trudy is moving 
toward the northwest near 9 mph (15 km/h). A general northwestward 
motion is expected today, followed by a turn toward the 
west-northwest tonight. On the forecast track, the center of Trudy 
will remain near the coast of southwestern and west-central Mexico 
through this evening and then move south of the Baja California 
Peninsula.
 
Maximum sustained winds remain near 100 mph (155 km/h) with higher
gusts. Some slight strengthening is possible this morning, but 
weakening is expected to begin late today. 
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 35 miles (55 km) from
the center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 140
miles (220 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 976 mb (28.82 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Trudy can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP1 and WMO header WTPZ41 KNHC
and on the web at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep1.shtml?key_messages.
 
WIND: Hurricane conditions are expected in the Hurricane Warning 
area this morning. Tropical storm conditions are expected within the 
mainland Mexico portion of the Tropical Storm Warning area this 
morning, and in the Islas Marias this afternoon and tonight. 
Hurricane conditions are possible in the Hurricane Watch area this 
morning.
 
RAINFALL: Through the weekend, Trudy is expected to produce 4 to 8
inches with isolated higher totals around 12 inches along and near
the southwest Mexican coast in Michoacán, Colima and Jalisco. This
rainfall may produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides,
especially in areas along steep terrain.
 
Elsewhere, Trudy’s outer bands are expected to produce 2 to 4 inch
amounts with isolated higher totals around 6 inches along the
southwest Mexican coast in Guerrero and Nayarit. This rainfall may
result in localized flash flooding, especially in areas along steep
terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Trudy,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep1.shtml?rainqpf.
 
STORM SURGE: A dangerous storm surge accompanied by damaging waves
is likely in areas of onshore winds within the warning areas.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Trudy are affecting portions of the coast 
of southwestern and west-central Mexico. These swells will cause 
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please consult 
products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 300 AM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Cangialosi

item.title: Hurricane Trudy Forecast Discussion Number 19
item.description:
Issued at 900 PM CST Sat Oct 17 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 180244
TCDEP1
 
Hurricane Trudy Discussion Number  19
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP212026
900 PM CST Sat Oct 17 2026
 
Over the last several hours the convection in the inner core of the 
cyclone has warmed slightly, though there are occasional hints of a 
ragged eye.  Looking at the most recent microwave data, Trudy 
appears to be affected by some southwesterly shear, given the 
northeastward tilt with height in the latest WSF-M pass. The 
initial intensity for the cyclone is being held at 85 kt based on 
a combination of recent objective and subjective estimates, and 
the initial position is adjusted somewhat to the west based on the 
microwave data. 
 
The hurricane is moving generally northwestward or 325 degrees/8 
kt. The cyclone should continue to move in an overall northwestward 
motion for the next 24-36 h as a weak low- to mid-level ridge 
builds over eastern Mexico. This continued motion would bring Trudy 
close to the coast of west-central Mexico overnight and Sunday. 
Afterwards, the hurricane is expected to weaken and then 
predominately be steered by low-level flow, which will result in a 
turn toward the west-northwest away from the coast. As mentioned 
before, the initial position has been adjusted farther west, thus 
the NHC track forecast has been moved slightly west as well. The 
current track forecast is still in good agreement with the HCCA and 
GDMI forecast aids. 
 
The environment around Trudy still supports some slight 
strengthening through the night, but southwesterly shear is likely 
to keep any strengthening limited.  By midday Sunday, an increase 
in southwesterly shear along with a decrease in mid-level relative 
humidity will result in a rapid weakening for Trudy. This weakening 
trend is expected to persist even as the cyclone moves away from 
the Mexican coast, and the new NHC forecast is lower than the last 
one. The current NHC intensity forecast has Trudy become 
post-tropical around 72 h, however it is possible that the cyclone 
could become post-tropical sooner based on the ECMWF simulated 
satellite guidance.  
 
 
KEY MESSAGES:
 
1. Trudy is forecast to strengthen as it moves near the coast of
southwestern and west-central Mexico tonight and Sunday. Damaging
hurricane-force winds are likely within the hurricane warning area.
 
2. A dangerous storm surge accompanied by damaging waves is likely
in areas of onshore winds within the warning areas.
 
3. Heavy rainfall associated with Trudy will impact the southwest 
Mexican coast between Guerrero and Nayarit through the weekend. This 
rainfall may produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides along 
and near the southwest Mexican coast in Michoacán, Colima, and 
Jalisco, especially in areas along steep terrain.
 
4. Large swells are affecting portions of the coast of southwestern
Mexico and will spread northward through the weekend, causing
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  18/0300Z 18.2N 105.7W   85 KT 100 MPH

 24H  19/0000Z 20.1N 107.1W   75 KT  85 MPH
